standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the morphism whose being an isomorphism of filtered objects is the second condition of the lemma.

standard_prerequisites.name: Kernels and cokernels of filtered objects
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the description of the filtration on the coimage as a quotient filtration and on the image as an induced filtration, which is what the proof compares.

core_obligations: The two filtrations (proof lines 4982-4989): the canonical morphism from the coimage of f to its image is an isomorphism of the underlying objects of the abelian category, and by the description of kernels and cokernels of filtered objects the filtration on the coimage is the quotient filtration coming from the map out of A while the filtration on the image is the induced filtration coming from the injection into B.

The equivalence (proof lines 4990-4992): strictness of f is defined by the coincidence of the quotient filtration with the induced filtration, and that coincidence is exactly the assertion that the canonical morphism is an isomorphism of filtered objects.
proof_roadmap: Recall that the canonical morphism between coimage and image is an isomorphism of the underlying objects.
Identify the two filtrations through the description of kernels and cokernels of filtered objects.
Read off the equivalence from the definition of strictness.
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that a morphism of filtered objects is strict exactly when the canonical morphism from its coimage to its image is an isomorphism of filtered objects (statement lines 4968-4979). The proof is a complete argument: the canonical morphism is already an isomorphism of the underlying objects, and the filtrations on the coimage and on the image are identified as the quotient filtration coming from the source and the induced filtration coming from the target, after which the equivalence follows from the definition of strictness (proof lines 4982-4992). The non-formal content is the identification of the two filtrations. The claim is H2: a structured argument with each input named.
